back: The predetermined cost of one unit, built from standard quantities and standard prices or rates.
A costing system that compares actual cost with standard cost and reports the variances for investigation.
A record of the standard quantity, price and cost of each element of one unit, with the standard selling price and profit.
Assumes perfect conditions: no waste, idle time or breakdowns. Usually gives adverse variances and demotivates.
An efficient but achievable standard that allows for normal waste and rest. Usually the most motivating.
A current standard reflects present conditions and prices. A basic standard is left unchanged for a long time and shows trends.
Σ (standard quantity × standard price) for materials + standard hours × standard rate for labour + overhead absorbed per unit.
Compare actual cost with the standard cost of the actual output, not with the original budget.
Only significant variances are investigated, so management time is spent where it matters.
